title: Inna and Its Sisters — Attached Pronouns (إِنَّهُ)

steps.title: A pronoun instead of a noun
body: Every sister of إنّ needs a subject right after it — so far you've only seen a full noun in that spot. But the subject can just as easily be a pronoun, attached directly to the particle. It's not a new set of endings: it's the exact same possessive suffixes you already know from gr:attached-possessive — ـهُ (his/him/it), ـهَا (her/it), ـكَ (your, m.), ـكِ (your, f.) — just landing on a particle instead of a noun.

إِنَّهُ سَعِيدٌ ("indeed he is happy") attaches ـهُ straight onto إِنَّ, doing the same job a following noun's accusative form would. سَمِعْتُ أَنَّهَا سَعِيدَةٌ ("I heard that she is happy") attaches ـهَا to أَنَّ instead — same mechanic, different sister.

The mechanic works identically on every one of the ten sisters, not just إِنَّ and أَنَّ: هُوَ سَعِيدٌ لِأَنَّهُ فِي الْبَيْتِ ("he is happy because he is at home") attaches ـهُ to لِأَنَّ. One irregularity worth flagging for later: the 1st-person suffix doesn't attach the expected way here — إِنَّ + ي actually surfaces as إِنِّي, not إِنَّنِي — but that's a detail for another day, not something this lesson asks you to produce.

steps.title: Three sisters, one pronoun mechanic
steps.intro: Read each sentence and find the attached pronoun riding on the sister of إنّ. Tap 🔊 to hear any line.

steps.title: Which noun is missing?
steps.prompt: There's no separate noun in this sentence at all. What is playing the role of اِسْم إِنَّ?

options.label: The attached pronoun ـهُ, built directly onto إِنَّ
Nothing — the sentence is missing its subject

steps.explanation: ـهُ is not decoration — it IS إِنَّ's subject here, exactly the role a following noun would otherwise play.

steps.title: A familiar suffix, a new host
steps.prompt: Where have you seen the suffix ـهَا before, attached to something else?

options.label: On a possessed noun — بَيْتُهَا, "her house"
Nowhere — this is the first time ـهَا has appeared
Only on verbs, never on nouns

steps.explanation: ـهَا is the same "her" suffix from gr:attached-possessive (بَيْتُهَا, "her house") — here it attaches to أَنَّ instead of a noun, but it's the identical suffix doing an analogous job.

steps.title: Every sister, not just two
steps.prompt: لِأَنَّهُ shows the attached-pronoun mechanic on a sister other than إِنَّ or أَنَّ. What does that tell you?

options.label: The mechanic applies to all ten sisters of إنّ, not just two of them
لِأَنَّ is a special exception that behaves differently from the rest
Only sisters that mean "that" can take a pronoun

steps.explanation: Any sister of إنّ — إِنَّ, أَنَّ, لِأَنَّ, كَأَنَّ, لٰكِنَّ, لَعَلَّ, or لَيْتَ — can take an attached pronoun in exactly the same way.

steps.title: إنّ's family, fully covered
steps.message: A following noun or an attached pronoun — either can be the subject of any sister of إنّ, and both take the same accusative role. Object-relative clauses and joining ideas into paragraphs are still ahead for this unit.
